_fixture: NOT OWNED HARDWARE. Exercises the linear-actuator type, which before ADR-0025
could not be recorded at all: the word 'force' did not occur in the schema.
It is still PARTIAL, and the note says exactly which published figures have no
home. The difference from before is qualitative rather than one of degree - the
headline figure can now be written down, where previously nothing could.

source.citation: Actuonix L12 specifications, 210:1 gear ratio at 12 V: 'Max Force (lifted)' 80 N, stall current 246 mA. Recorded as a stall figure because it is what the actuator can move a load with at the limit, not what it can sustain - see duty_cycle_pct.

Actuonix L12 is sold in 50:1, 100:1 and 210:1 gear ratios; this fixture takes the 210:1, whose published figures are 62 N at 3.2 mm/s peak power point, 6.5 mm/s max no-load speed, 80 N max force lifted and 45 N back drive force.

Actuonix L12 general specifications: 12 VDC nominal with a 13.5 V maximum input, stall current 246 mA at 12 V. A 6 VDC variant is sold with different force figures, which is why at_volts is the index.

Actuonix L12 Miniature Linear Motion Series, 100 mm stroke, 210:1, 12 V, potentiometer feedback. Figures read 2026-08-23 from vendor and retailer specification listings, confirmed across two independent searches. The manufacturer's own PDF datasheet could NOT be text-extracted - it uses subset fonts with an unmapped encoding, the third datasheet this session to resist reading for a third distinct reason.

note:
WHY continuous_force_n IS NULL, AND FOR ONCE THE VENDOR SAYS SO. Actuonix publishes 'Max Duty Cycle: 20%'. That is a manufacturer stating in as many words that the published forces are not continuous ratings, which is more than either servo vendor offered. It is recorded in duty_cycle_pct rather than left to prose, because it is the reason a reader should not reach for the 80 N.

FOUR PUBLISHED FIGURES STILL HAVE NO HOME, and naming them is half the point of this fixture:

  Back Drive Force (static) 45 N   - the force needed to back-drive it unpowered.
                                     ADR-0021 gave rotary actuators
                                     gearbox.backdriving_torque_nm, as a RANGE. The
                                     linear equivalent wants the same treatment and
                                     should get it in the same ADR as the rotary one,
                                     not bolted on here.
  Max Static Force 200 N           - what it can WITHSTAND while not moving. A
                                     structural rating, not an output. No rotary
                                     analogue exists in this schema either.
  Peak Power Point 62 N @ 3.2 mm/s - a force paired with a speed, i.e. one point on a
                                     curve. Same shape as measured_efficiency.
  Max Speed (no load) 6.5 mm/s     - no_load_speed_rad_s is ANGULAR. A linear
                                     actuator's no-load speed is mm/s and there is no
                                     field for it.

And mechanical backlash 0.2 mm cannot go in gearbox.backlash_rad for the same reason: that field is radians.

SO THE SCHEMA IS ROTARY-SHAPED THROUGHOUT, and force was the largest of several mismatches rather than the only one. ADR-0025 fixed the headline deliberately and named the rest rather than making five decisions in one afternoon.
